title: Dissipation in Periodically Driven Quantum Systems: Partial Secularization and Thermodynamic Consistency
authors: Luísa T. Tude, Carlos Ortega-Taberner, Roberta Zambrini, Gonzalo Manzano
abstract: Periodically driven open quantum systems are central to quantum thermodynamics and quantum control. These systems are typically described using Floquet-Born-Markov master equations, derived with the use of a full secular approximation, and whose thermodynamic implications are often overlooked. In this context, we show that such a strong secular approximation may lead to unphysical predictions for steady state energy currents. We then demonstrate that a coarse-grained formulation of the master equation can regularize these issues while yielding completely positive dynamics and consistent energy currents. The coarse-graining time has a clear physical interpretation, as it defines the temporal resolution at which a Markovian master equation can describe the evolution of the periodically driven system. We show the consistency and validity of our approach by comparing to an exact non-Markovian simulation in paradigmatic examples: a driven two-level system and a three-level maser coupled to hot and cold thermal reservoirs. Our work provides a practical framework for correctly applying the secular approximation in periodically driven-dissipative systems and for assessing the accuracy of master equations of the GKSL form.
summary: This paper tackles the failure of standard master equation approximations when modeling open quantum systems under periodic driving. The authors introduce a coarse-graining technique that regularizes these models, ensuring thermodynamic consistency for calculated energy currents. This framework offers a practical way to validate the accuracy of Markovian descriptions in non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The study addresses unphysical predictions for steady-state energy currents that arise when applying a strong secular approximation to master equations describing periodically driven open quantum systems.
main_result: A coarse-grained formulation of the master equation successfully regularizes these thermodynamic inconsistencies, yielding completely positive dynamics and consistent energy current calculations.
method: The authors propose a coarse-graining approach applied to the Floquet-Redfield master equation, which allows for partial secularization while maintaining physical consistency.
model_or_system: The system involves open quantum systems subjected to periodic driving, modeled by Hamiltonians $H(t) = H_S(t) + H_B + H_{SB}$. The dynamics are analyzed using Floquet-Born-Markov master equations.
key_observables: Steady state energy currents (work and heat contributions), complete positivity of evolution, and the coarse-graining time interval ($	au_{CG}$).
important_parameters: The driving period $T$, coupling strengths ($\lambda$), and characteristic timescales are key parameters used to assess approximation validity.
main_assumptions: The standard approach relies on Born and Markov approximations; the proposed method introduces a coarse-graining time $	au_{CG}$ to regularize these issues.
figures_summary: Figure 9 compares RWA vs. exact dynamics for off-diagonal elements, period-averaged steady-state populations, and energy flow during a cycle.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem with the full secular approximation leading to thermodynamic inconsistencies; it then introduces the coarse-grained master equation approach, demonstrating its consistency by comparing results against exact non-Markovian simulations for specific examples like driven two-level systems and masers.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial theoretical tool for correctly applying approximations (like secularization) in complex, periodically driven quantum systems relevant to quantum thermodynamics and energy harvesting.
